text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service=redwood-runtime-prod, incident=PD-98321, severity=P1
incident-bot: symptom=5xx spike on /v1/generate, region=us-west-2, rolling 1m error rate=12% (>5% threshold)
incident-bot: affected-customers=3 (high-traffic accounts), estimated-error-requests=~2.4k/min
incident-bot: recommended action: page primary on-call, evaluate fallback to smaller model, consider routing to dedicated nodes

pagerduty: PagerDuty notification: PD-98321 triggered from policy "critical-runtime-errors"
PagerDuty: Primary on-call: @alice (10m to ack threshold). Secondary: @bob. Manager escalation: @carol.

alice: acked the page — investigating now :eyes:
alice: quick check — metrics -> CPU/GPU usage normal, but inference queue length for runtime-worker group xlarge-1 is growing
alice: grabbing recent logs from the serving tier

alice: logs show repeated kv-cache eviction errors and OOMs in worker-3, sample trace:
```
2026-03-14T03:42:10Z runtime-worker-3 ERROR kv_cache.cpp:245 evict failed: insufficient memory
2026-03-14T03:42:11Z runtime-worker-3 WARN decode.cpp:88 decode slowdown, token_time=230ms
2026-03-14T03:42:12Z runtime-worker-3 ERROR llama_kernel: cudnnLaunchKernel failed: out of memory
```

alice: hypothesis: a memory regression in the recent runtime kernel build with long prefix use, causing thrashing -> queue buildup -> 5xx

bob: i've pulled the canary logs too — same OOMs around same time. can we rollback kernel?

dave: reproduction on staging? i can spin a job with long prefixes but need to be quick

alice: quick mitigation plan: 1) reduce concurrency config on runtime-worker pool (scale down threads) 2) force fallback to quantized model variant for affected customers 3) spin up extra dedicated nodes in us-west-2 as temporary capacity

eve: prefilling cache might help but takes time. recommend (2) and (3) as quickest wins.

alice: i'm applying a temporary routing rule to send heavy request patterns to dedicated pool: `/ops/routing set route regex \u005c\u005c\u005cb(long_context) -> dedicated-pool-usw2-temp`

incident-bot: routing rule applied by alice at 03:46 UTC

alice: reducing runtime-worker concurrency from 16 -> 8 on xlarge-1 group (rolling restart)

pagerduty: ack not detected for secondary within 10m — escalation in 1m

bob: secondary is up; taking over if primary needs eyes. I'm starting a targeted rollback of the kernel build on two worker hosts now.

incident-bot: PagerDuty escalation: PD-98321 escalated to manager @carol after missed ack window on secondary (policy: escalate_after=11m)

carol: on it — joining call. please post customer impact summary and ETA for mitigation

alice: impact: 3 paying customers experiencing intermittent 5xxs on generation endpoints, internal monitoring shows SLO error budget burn for one account. We have routing in place to offload 60% of traffic to dedicated pool.

bob: rollback of kernel started on worker-3 and worker-4, each will take ~90s to restart and rejoin.

bob: restart done on worker-3, logs show no OOMs post-boot, error rate on that host dropped from 18% -> 1.5%

alice: rolling restart 3/6 complete. global 5xx rate down from 12% -> 6% after first hosts rejoined. still above threshold.

carol: good progress. are any customers still seeing errors? which accounts & severity? need comms if ETA >20m

alice: account list: acct-alpha (high traffic) — intermittent failures, acct-beta — degraded latency but mostly ok, acct-gamma — experiencing 5xxs.

alice: ETA to full remediation if rollback continues on remaining hosts: ~12-18 minutes. If we need faster, we can enable full model-fallback for affected accounts (will change quality).

eve: ops note: enabling model-fallback requires feature-flag flip and a short config propagation (~90s) — quality drop expected ~10-15% on some prompts

carol: notify customer success for acct-alpha and acct-gamma with heads-up for degraded service and ETA 20m. Use proactive template.

alice: leaving primary-ack; handing to @bob for follow-up — i'm switching to wrap-up on other pages.

bob: taking over. continuing rollback and watching error rate and latency dashboards.

incident-bot: PD-98321 note: manager-escalation acknowledged by @carol at 03:58 UTC

bob: last two hosts rolled. cluster error rate now 0.9% across us-west-2. tail latencies back to normal.

alice: great. revert routing rule in 5m after we confirm stability

incident-bot: escalation policy action complete. paging history: primary ack by alice, secondary ack by bob, manager escalation triggered and acknowledged by carol.

carol: postmortem required: assign to eng-runtime, tag regression -> kernel-release-2026-03-14, severity=P1? we'll decide after RCA.

bob: filing short incident summary now and will include timeline + mitigations + config diffs.

alice: thumbs up. i'll loop in support & CS for customer follow-ups.

eve: followup checklist — (1) verify no reoccurrence in 2h (2) roll forward fix or revert permanently (3) test long-prefix workloads on staging with debug builds (4) add guardrail for memory regression by nightly mem-check job

carol: agreed. set a 2h post-incident review. assigning owners: bob (rollback & RCA), alice (customer comms), eve (monitoring guardrails).

bob: marking PD incident resolved in PagerDuty once we've had steady state 5m with <1% errors.

incident-bot: note: incident-thread will be archived after the incident is closed. thanks everyone :heart:
